scope: From the manifesto: "The American lawn is not a neutral aesthetic choice. It is an enforced land use regime—backed by HOA covenants, municipal weed ordinances, chemical industry lobbying, and a century of suburban ideology—that converts potentially productive, biodiverse, community-serving land into sterile, performative monoculture. It is an enclosure. It should be abolished." In scope: the rules that enforce lawns (HOA covenants, weed and grass-height ordinances, state laws preempting or protecting them, enforcement cases); what lawns cost (water, pesticides and fertilizer, fuel and emissions from equipment, the lawn care industry); what they displace or could become (native plantings, food, habitat, pollinators, stormwater); changes that loosen the regime (turf-removal rebates, nonfunctional-turf bans, gas equipment rules, native-landscaping laws); and new research on any of it. National and international, with US state and local law at the center.
